audit_note: WIC 16001.9(a)(27) on the page says 'to immediate enrollment upon a change of school', which matches 'enroll right away'.
WIC 16010.4(d)(10) lists 'A copy of the health and education summary as required under Section 16010' and (d)(9) lists a plan of the child's needs, so the tip is supported.
Rule 8.450(e)(4)(A) on the page gives the 7-day notice of intent deadline, which supports 'deadlines are short'.
The relatives guide says 'Make sure to contact the social worker. Don't wait for the social worker to contact you.'

WIC 317(e)(2) on the page says counsel 'shall advise the court of the child's wishes' and (e)(1) covers the child's interests; note the page limits the wishes duty to a child four or older, which the citation line does not say.
WIC 11363 says 'under 18 years of age' with listed exceptions to 19 or 21, so 'usually stop at 18' fits the page.
WIC 349(c) on the page says the court 'shall inform the minor or nonminor dependent that they have the right to address the court' when they are present.
Booklet pages 9-10 say the judge will 'Decide where your child should live (this is called placement)' and decide what services you need.
Booklet page 9 says 'the court will take authority over your child. This is called jurisdiction in the law'.
Booklet page 29 has the exact legal custody sentence about medical care, school, and religion.
Booklet page 16 says 'Once an adoption is final, it cannot be changed no matter what you do' and that the court terminates parental rights.

WIC 361(a)(1) has the quoted 'limits the right of the parent...' wording for school decisions, and the parents Self-Help Guide says you keep education and health care decisions; note 361(a) itself does not mention health.

WIC 366.26(c)(4)(B) says a child 16 or older or a nonminor dependent may get 'another planned permanent living arrangement' when no other permanent plan fits; the entry skips the fit and willing relative option but the meaning holds.
The children guide says to call the county agency main number and ask for a supervisor, and 'You can also let your lawyer know'.
The parents guide says 'These court hearings are dependency status review (DSR) hearings' and lists other names for review hearings.
The CDSS page says THP gives supports 'to successfully transition to independence while reducing the risks of homelessness'.
The parents guide says 'If you cannot afford a lawyer, the judge will assign one to you.'
WIC 342(a) says that when a minor is already found to be described by Section 300 and new facts are alleged, 'the petitioner shall file a subsequent petition'.
WIC 362(a) says that when a child is adjudged a dependent the court 'may make any and all reasonable orders for the care, supervision, custody, conduct, maintenance, and support of the child'.
WIC 300(g) lists 'left without any provision for support' as its own ground with no 'parent cannot be located' test, plus other grounds the entry leaves out, so the entry conflicts with the page.
WIC 366.26(b)(7) says 'Order that the child remain in foster care' with conditions and review, and the words 'long-term foster care' are nowhere in the section.

WIC 300(b)(1) has the quoted failure to supervise or protect text and lists substance abuse in (D); note the page ties substance abuse to being unable to give regular care and lists other causes the entry skips.
WIC 16001.9(a)(28) gives access to information on 'the coursework necessary for career, technical, and postsecondary educational programs'.
WIC 16001.9(a)(2) reads 'To be free from physical, sexual, emotional, or other abuse, corporal punishment, and exploitation.'

The quote is on the page, but WIC 16001.9(a)(12) limits family contact only when 'prohibited by court order'; the app says 'unless unsafe', which is a different test and does not say a judge must order it.
The parents guide says at the first hearing 'If you cannot afford a lawyer, the judge will assign one to you.'
Booklet page 8 says your attorney gives you a paper called a petition that lists the allegations; the booklet does not call this a 'right' in those words.
Booklet page 10 lists 'a drug rehab program, parenting classes, counseling, or anger management classes'; note the booklet never uses the words 'service provider'.

Rule 5.695(f)(3) has the exact 'the court must order visitation...' sentence and says visits are to be as frequent as possible; the where and conditions details are not on this page but nothing conflicts.
WIC 366(a)(1) says review 'no less frequently than once every six months' and the court looks at the need for placement and progress toward fixing the causes.
WIC 355(a) has the exact preponderance sentence for the jurisdictional hearing; note the page does not name the county as the one who must prove it.
Rule 5.530(b)(2) lists 'All parents, de facto parents, Indian custodians, and guardians of the child' as entitled to be present.
WIC 319(f)(3) and (h)(2) have the quoted relative wording and relative preference; note the page calls the detention placement temporary and does not itself tell relatives to speak up.
WIC 346 says 'the public shall not be admitted to a juvenile court hearing' but the judge may admit people with a direct and legitimate interest.
WIC 366.21(g)(4) and (h) have both quoted parts on setting a 366.26 hearing within 120 days and ending services; note (g)(1) also lets the judge give up to 6 more months first.
WIC 16501.1(g)(16)(A)(i) puts adult-life planning in the case plan at 14 or 15, and the TILP comes at 16, so 'starts at 16' conflicts with the page.
WIC 366.22(a) says the 18-month hearing either returns the child or sets a 366.26 hearing within 120 days to pick the plan, so the plan is not usually finalized at this hearing.
The site says 'Family Urgent Response System (formerly known as Cal-FURS)' and serves current or former foster youth and caregivers.
The Title 3 PDF shows fee waiver rules running 3.50 to 'Rule 3.58. Posting notice', with 3.60-3.63 only as old numbers; the Gov. Code part is not on this page.
The relatives guide says 'The judge is required to consider letting you visit the child if it is in the child's best interest', and also that the judge does not have to allow it.

The relatives guide has the quoted exemption sentence and says to talk to the social worker or a lawyer about it; the page says the social worker gets the exemption, and does not use the words 'apply' or 'right away'.
Rule 5.534(j) is 'Electronic service address'; 'Caregiver notice and right to be heard' with form JV-290 is (k), so the cited letter is wrong.
WIC 16501 defines child welfare services and has the quoted 'supportive transition services' phrase, but says nothing about a youth's right to prepare for adulthood, a TILP, or age 14.
The contact page uses 'California Office of the Foster Care Ombudsperson' in the logo text and body, and the word 'Ombudsman' is not on the page.

Ed Code 48853.5(f)(1) says the school 'shall allow the foster child to continue' in the school of origin, and (f)(6) needs agreement only to waive that right, so the entry has the condition backwards.
25 U.S.C. 1915(b)(i) puts 'a member of the Indian child's extended family' first with no Native requirement, and 1903(2) defines that by relationship; the entry's 'Native family members' narrows it.
WIC 388(a)(1) says 'upon grounds of change of circumstance or new evidence', and rule 5.570(b) says the petition must be on form JV-180.

The quote is on the page, but WIC 362(d) also lets the court 'direct any reasonable orders to the parents or guardians' as 'necessary and proper', so a home safety order does not conflict with it; the entry is loose or unsupported in its wording, not WRONG.

The quote is on booklet page 24, but the booklet never says who writes the case plan; the conflict shows in WIC 358(b)(1), which says the social worker's report 'shall include the individual child's case plan', so the link should point there.
